name: Crucible Fab-Floor Apprentice Daily Rig
description:
The standard daily kit for apprentice-grade workers on Crucible Industries' fabrication floors — one step below full technician, assigned to feed lines, operate basic presses, and assist with materials handling. The centerpiece is a flame-resistant coverall in Crucible's corporate deep red, overlaid with charcoal grey panels at the thighs and chest for reinforcement. The Crucible triangular logo is heat-bonded in silver on the upper back and left chest; a name patch in white sits above the right breast. The coverall's left sleeve has an aug channel — a velcro-and-snap seam that allows the sleeve to be peeled back or removed entirely for workers with forearm chrome, a mandatory accommodation on all Crucible fab-floor issue since the 2189 labor compact. The collar is high-cut with a chin guard snap for respirator attachment. Beneath the coverall, a heat-dispersing base layer in light grey manages thermal output from proximity to active machinery. Safety boots are Crucible-issued Penrose Weld Boots — steel-shank, heat-resistant sole, composite toe. A hard-shell safety helmet in the same deep red carries a flip-down UV-filter visor and a small rear port for BCI hard-line connection to the floor network. Insulated synth-leather work gloves clip to the coverall's chest ring when not in use.

Apprentices often mark their helmets with small stickers or hand-scratched tallies tracking shift counts toward their journeyman certification — an unofficial tradition the floor supervisors quietly tolerate. The coverall's deep red marks them instantly as Crucible property in motion through Circuit's streets, which carries both the protection of corponation affiliation and the occasional hostility from workers employed by rival fabricators.
functionality: Flame and heat resistance, aug-channel sleeve for forearm chrome access, respirator collar attachment, BCI hard-line port on helmet for floor network integration, UV-filter visor, heat-dispersing underlayer, composite steel-toe welding boots
what_it_says: Employed, certified by a major corponation, working toward something. The apprentice kit is less prestigious than a full technician's rig but miles above the Shelf — it represents a rung on a ladder that actually goes somewhere.
story_hooks: A Crucible apprentice's helmet tally marks show 847 shifts — far more than the 500 required for journeyman certification. Someone has been blocking their advancement, and they've stopped asking why.
The floor network BCI port on a worker's helmet was used to pull unauthorized schematics during a night shift; the access log shows the port ID, and the helmet is still in the locker room.
A character in a stolen Crucible apprentice kit tries to access the fab floor — but the corponation's biometric door system checks more than the uniform.
